classification.summary: CorkHook.beforeSwap() was callable by anyone rather than only by the Uniswap v4 PoolManager, so the attacker forced a CorkCall callback into ModuleCore's PSM for a market they had created with an existing market's DS token as its redemption asset, double-counting the FlashSwapRouter's DS balance and minting redeemable CT/DS against the real wstETH reserves.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

sources.note: onchain review: CorkHook 0x5287E8915445aee78e10190559D8Dd21E0E9Ea88 is a non-upgradeable contract created by Cork's CREATE3 deployer 0x777777727073e72fbb3c81f9a8b88cc49feae2f5 (not the attacker) and emits 5 logs inside the attack tx; the drained ModuleCore proxy 0xCCd90F6435dd78C4ECCED1FA4db0D7242548a2a9 emitted PsmDeposited, InitializedModuleCore and Issued in the same tx and is recorded here as the funds-losing contract rather than the flaw site (its implementation had been upgraded 3h32m earlier, so measuring from it would understate the age of the exploited code)
